project_title: US Census Data Cleaning & EDA Cheat Sheet

code_patterns.explanation: Uses Regular Expressions to gather all file paths starting with 'states_' and ending in '.csv'.
`lapply` applies `read_csv` across all file paths into a list, and `bind_rows` stacks them vertically into one unified data frame.

code_patterns.code_example:
us_census <- us_census %>%
  mutate(
    Income = str_remove_all(Income, "[\\$\\,]"),
    Hispanic = str_remove(Hispanic, "%\\")
  )
code_patterns.explanation: Strips currency symbols (`$`, `,`) and percent signs (`%`) from target character columns.

code_patterns.code_example:
race_cols <- c('Hispanic', 'White', 'Black', 'Native', 'Asian', 'Pacific')
us_census <- us_census %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(race_cols), ~ str_remove(.x, "%\\")))
code_patterns.explanation: Applies a regex stripping function to a predefined vector of column names simultaneously.

code_patterns.code_example:
us_census <- us_census %>%
  separate(GenderPop, into = c('male_pop', 'female_pop'), sep = "_") %>%
  mutate(
    male_pop = str_remove(male_pop, "M"),
    female_pop = str_remove(female_pop, "F")
  )
code_patterns.explanation: Splits `GenderPop` by delimiter `_` into distinct variables and strips character labels.

code_patterns.code_example:
num_cols <- c(race_cols, "Income", "male_pop", "female_pop")
us_census <- us_census %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(num_cols), as.numeric))
code_patterns.explanation: Converts specified character variables to standard double/numeric data types.
Converts integer/double percentages ($0-100$) into standard statistical proportions ($0.0-1.0$).
Identifies exact duplicate rows and retains only distinct records.

code_patterns.code_example:
us_census <- us_census %>%
  mutate(female_pop = if_else(is.na(female_pop), TotalPop - male_pop, female_pop))
code_patterns.explanation: Calculates missing female population figures using existing `TotalPop` and `male_pop` columns.

code_patterns.code_example:
us_census <- us_census %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(race_cols), ~ if_else(is.na(.x), median(.x, na.rm = TRUE), .x)))
code_patterns.explanation: Fills missing missing demographic entries using column-wide medians.

code_patterns.code_example:
census_long <- us_census %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(race_cols), names_to = "Race", values_to = "Proportion")
code_patterns.explanation: Transforms racial variables into key-value pairs suitable for faceted `ggplot2` visualizations.

code_patterns.code_example:
ggplot(us_census, aes(x = Income)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  theme_minimal()
code_patterns.explanation: Generates a binned histogram to display distribution metrics.

code_patterns.code_example:
ggplot(us_census, aes(x = Hispanic, y = Income)) +
  geom_point(color = "darkorange") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal()
code_patterns.explanation: Plots two continuous variables with an overlay regression trend line.
